hourly.summary: Arsenal fans are in full meltdown mode after a 3-0 humbling at Brighton ended their unbeaten start and title defence in brutal fashion. The consensus is this wasn't just a bad day at the office — it was a tactical and physical capitulation that's handed the rest of the league a blueprint for beating the Gunners. Arteta admitted he knew something was off from the first throw-in, while supporters are questioning summer business, midfield legs, and whether the squad has the mentality to bounce back. The only consolation? Spurs lost too. Small mercies.

daily.summary: Arsenal fan sentiment evolved from a placid morning lull to peak euphoria by midday following title celebrations and a flawless start, before settling into an evening buzz tempered by characteristic Gooner anxiety. The dominant arc traces quiet confidence giving way to Invincibles-adjacent elation, then a return to cautious optimism as transfer rumors and rival fixation resurface. Overall, the fanbase rides a high of competitive dominance across both teams, underscored by the perpetual fear that 'HaramBall' will disrupt the party.

weekly.summary: Arsenal fan sentiment started the week with high buoyancy and confidence but gradually deteriorated, culminating in an aggrieved mood by midweek as frustrations over officiating, defensive lapses, and the women's team's stumble grew. The overall trend shows a decline from optimistic to wary, with lingering concerns about consistency and external factors tempering optimism.
